observation: In Table 6 panel (b) the working-poor trade-off exceeds the demogrant trade-off for Finland (4.65 vs 4.10), Italy (1.84 vs 1.82) and Sweden (6.21 vs 4.30); these are reproduced faithfully and match the paper's own printed Table 6(b).
why_suspicious: The replication plan's expected outcome states the working-poor trade-off remains below the demogrant trade-off in EVERY country in panel (b). That is not what the paper's table shows (nor what the correct computation yields) for the three compressed-earnings-distribution countries. The paper's prose 'more favourable' refers to overall desirability/efficiency effect, not the trade-off ratio in every country. No code defect; flagging the plan-vs-paper mismatch.

observation: Denmark's demogrant trade-off in Table 6(b) reproduces as 28.10 vs the paper's 29.09 (~3% gap), whereas Table 2(a) Denmark reproduces exactly (25.25).
why_suspicious: The trade-off denominator pg*(1-Dd)-sg is near-singular for Denmark (very large trade-off), so it amplifies small differences in how the heterogeneous eta profile weights the group-decile cells.
